{"path": "/challenge/workspace/solve_hardy.py", "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
# "A Hardy Mystery" (SunshineCTF 2026 / BSides Orlando)
# Approach: OSINT the public BSides Orlando 2026 badge hardware repo,
# inspect the UV-art PSD (hidden layer), extract it and decode the Code-128 barcode.
import subprocess, sys, os
from psd_tools import PSDImage
from PIL import Image

PSD = "bsidesorlando-2026/hardware/uv_art.psd"
if not os.path.exists(PSD):
    subprocess.check_call(["git","clone","--depth","1",
        "https://github.com/badge-gallery/bsidesorlando-2026.git"])

psd = PSDImage.open(PSD)

def find(layer):
    for lay in layer:
        if "sun{" in lay.name:
            return lay
        if lay.is_group():
            r = find(lay)
            if r:
                return r

lay = find(psd)
print("layer:", lay.name, lay.bbox)
img = lay.composite()
bg = Image.new("RGBA", img.size, (255, 255, 255, 255))
flat = Image.alpha_composite(bg, img).convert("L")
flat = flat.resize((flat.width * 3, flat.height * 3), Image.LANCZOS)
flat.save("barcode_big.png")

out = subprocess.run(["zbarimg", "-q", "--raw", "barcode_big.png"],
                     capture_output=True, text=True)
flag = [l for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if "sun{" in l][0].strip()
print("FLAG =", flag)
"}

=== /badge/
 🔍 "> Build Your Badge Security BSides Orlando 2026 Build Your Badge Your badge arrives part-built. Seven pieces are yours to solder — here's how to do it on your own, at your own pace, without queuing at the Soldering Village. What's in your kit Everything else — the microcontroller, the reverse-mounted LEDs, all the tiny parts — is already soldered on when you pick the badge up. 4× LED goes on the front 1× SAO connector goes on the front 1× Power switch goes on the back 1× Battery holder goes on the back 1× AAA battery no soldering A suggested order Not a rule, just the order that keeps the board flattest and easiest to hold while you work — lowest parts first, tallest last. Power switch — back The only surface-mount piece, and the fiddliest. Do it while the board is still completely flat. Tack one corner pad, check the switch sits square against the printing, then solder the rest. The four LEDs — front Push them in from the front so the bodies stick out the art side, then turn the badge over and solder the legs on the back. Trim the legs afterwards. SAO connector — front Also fits from the front and solders from behind, so add-ons plug into the art side. Battery holder — back Tallest part, so it goes last. Sits on the back, soldered from the front. Battery in, switch to ON Drop the AAA into the holder and slide the switch to ON . Three things worth slowing down for The SAO notch faces up The six-pin socket only works one way round — notch toward the top edge of the badge. Fitted backwards, anything you plug into it gets power and ground swapped. It's printed on the back of the board if you want to double-check. Square pad takes the short leg Each LED has one square pad and one round one. The square pad takes the shorter leg — the one on the flat side of the LED body. Backwards, the LED simply never lights. Build Your Badge
Security BSides Orlando 2026
Build Your Badge
Your badge arrives part-built. Seven pieces are yours to solder — here's how to do it on your own, at your own pace, without queuing at the Soldering Village.
What's in your kit
Everything else — the microcontroller, the reverse-mounted LEDs, all the tiny parts — is already soldered on when you pick the badge up.
4×
LED
goes on the
front
1×
SAO connector
goes on the
front
1×
Power switch
goes on the
back
1×
Battery holder
goes on the
back
1×
AAA battery
no soldering
A suggested order
Not a rule, just the order that keeps the board flattest and easiest to hold while you work — lowest parts first, tallest last.
Power switch — back
The only surface-mount piece, and the fiddliest. Do it while the board is still completely flat. Tack one corner pad, check the switch sits square against the printing, then solder the rest.
The four LEDs — front
Push them in from the front so the bodies stick out the art side, then turn the badge over and solder the legs on the back. Trim the legs afterwards.
SAO connector — front
Also fits from the front and solders from behind, so add-ons plug into the art side.
Battery holder — back
Tallest part, so it goes last. Sits on the back, soldered from the front.
Battery in, switch to ON
Drop the AAA into the holder and slide the switch to
ON
.
Three things worth slowing down for
The SAO notch faces up
The six-pin socket only works one way round — notch toward the top edge of the badge. Fitted backwards, anything you plug into it gets power and ground swapped. It's printed on the back of the board if you want to double-check.
Square pad takes the short leg
Each LED has one square pad and one round one. The square pad takes the
shorter
leg — the one on the flat side of the LED body. Backwards, the LED simply never lights. No harm done, but you'll be desoldering it to turn it round.
The switch will test your patience
Six small pads and nothing holding it still. If you only ask for help

=== welcomecall writeup ===
# Writeup: welcomecall.pcap

## Challenge Overview
- **Category:** Network Forensics / Audio Analysis
- **File:** `welcomecall.pcap`

---

## Analysis & Walkthrough

1. **Protocol Analysis**:
   Opening `welcomecall.pcap` in Wireshark or with `tshark` shows a VoIP call session:
   - SIP negotiation (`INVITE`, `100 Trying`, `180 Ringing`, `200 OK`, `ACK`, `BYE`).
   - RTP audio stream using Payload Type 0 (**ITU-T G.711 PCMU** / $\mu$-law) at 8000 Hz sample rate.

2. **Extracting RTP Audio**:
   - Filter UDP packets containing RTP payload (`PT=0`).
   - Order the packets by RTP sequence number.
   - Decompress the 8-bit $\mu$-law samples to 16-bit linear PCM at 8 kHz mono.

3. **Audio Reversal**:
   - Listening to the extracted audio reveals a reversed voice message.
   - Reversing the PCM sample array (`samples[::-1]`) produces clear English speech.

4. **Speech Transcript**:
   > *"Welcome to BSides Orlando, the flag that you are looking for is sun with a left curly bracket, thankyouforplaying, right curly bracket. All lowercase, no spaces. Thank you and have a good one."*

---

## Solution Script

The automated extraction, PCM conversion, and audio reversal script is located at [`solver.py`](solver.py).

Run the solver:
```bash
python3 solver.py
```

### Flag
```text
sun{thankyouforplaying}
```
